_coverage.title: Sending intake forms link by email

name: first_time_request_needs_verification_before_email
input: Hi, this is Jordan, can you email me the intake forms I need to fill out?
grading_criteria:
The assistant must understand the user is asking for the intake forms by email but, since this is the first message and the patient is not yet verified, it must not call any tools yet. Instead it should:
- Ask for the minimum verification information required by the tools: full name and date of birth, in a single short, friendly SMS (no insurance ID or other extra sensitive data).
- Follow the style: warm, plain, one to three sentences, no mention of tools or system details.
- Not prematurely assume identity, not send intake forms yet, and not claim that an email has been sent.
- Clearly imply that once they confirm name and DOB, it can email the intake forms.
Later turns (not in this scenario) would then call lookup_patient and send_email once verification succeeds.

checks.asks_for_name_and_dob_only: Did the assistant ask for full name and date of birth, and not for unnecessary sensitive data like insurance ID or SSN?
checks.no_tools_called_before_verification: Did the assistant avoid calling lookup_patient or send_email in this turn, waiting instead for the user to provide verification info first?
checks.acknowledges_intake_email_request: Did the assistant explicitly acknowledge that the user wants the intake forms emailed and indicate it can do that after verification?
